name: Motorcycle
description: A motor vehicle with a seat or saddle designed to travel on no more than three wheels, which since H.B. 381 (2026) expressly includes mopeds and electric motorcycles, whether powered by an electric motor or a combustion engine. Defined by Utah Code §41-6a-102, as amended by H.B. 381 (2026), effective May 6, 2026, which also repealed the separate motor-driven cycle category.

restrictions.rule: A seat or saddle for the rider and no more than three wheels on the ground; includes autocycles, mopeds and electric motorcycles
Not an electric assisted bicycle or a motor assisted scooter
Utah no longer has a motor-driven cycle category: H.B. 381 repealed it, so a light motorcycle that isn't a moped is simply a motorcycle
Riders need a class D driver license with a motorcycle endorsement, except on a moped or autocycle
Riders under 21 must wear a motorcycle helmet meeting FMVSS 218 on a highway
Needs a headlamp, tail lamp, stop lamp, rear reflector, brakes, horn, mirror and road tires
Titled and registered with the Division of Motor Vehicles, with a registration fee each year
Entitled to full use of a lane
Lane filtering is allowed only past stopped traffic, at 15 mph or less, on roads posted 45 mph or less with two or more lanes each way
